title: Local bijectivity of Hom comparisons implies local bijectivity on Isom
statement: Let (C,J) be a small site, R a ring sheaf, D a category, and F:D→Mod(R) [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category] a functor. For M,N in D define cMN from the constant presheaf of Hom_D(M,N) to H(FM,FN) [lem-sf-local-module-hom-sheaf] by restriction of F(f). Define cIso analogously from constant Isom_D(M,N) to localIso(FM,FN) [lem-sf-local-module-isom-sheaf]. If cMN is locally injective and locally surjective, cNM is locally surjective, and cMM,cNN are locally injective, then cIso is locally injective and locally surjective.

proof.text: The constant Hom maps are natural because restrictions evaluate the same component of F(f). They preserve composition and identities by the functor laws of F and overFunctor. Define the constant Isom map by overFunctor.mapIso(F.mapIso a). Its hom and inverse correspond to cMN(a.hom) and cNM(a.inv).

If two constant isomorphisms have the same image, their hom maps have the same image under cMN. Local injectivity of cMN gives a covering equalizer sieve for these hom maps. Iso.ext then gives equality of the isomorphisms on that covering sieve.

Given a local isomorphism e, intersect the covering image sieves of its hom and inverse to lift them simultaneously to g:M→N and h:N→M. The images of gh and hg are the two identities because the Hom comparisons respect composition. Local injectivity of cMM and cNN gives two covering equality sieves; intersect them. On that refinement g,h are inverse in D, so define an actual isomorphism lifting the restriction of e. Use naturality of cMN and of the localIso-to-localHom map to verify the image equality. Transitivity of J makes the image sieve of e covering.
